newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two Russia oil companies plan debt restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Two Russia oil companies plan debt restructuring.

text.p: Russian oil companies Yuganskneftegaz and Samaraneftegaz will use a government debt restructuring scheme to make a bond issue equal to the size of their debts to the state, the companies said on Thursday.

"The government order No. 254 (outlining the restructuring scheme) gave us the light at the end of the tunnel," Mikhail Khodorkovsky, chairman of the Rosprom-YUKOS industrial group, told a news conference after a shareholders meeting.
Yuganskneftegaz and Samaraneftegaz are subsidiaries of oil group YUKOS, which is allied with Bank Menatep's Rosprom group in a combined management structure.
"We are planning to pay off our debts to the government over two years and to pay off fines over five years," he said.
The government's proposals allow companies owing money to the state to securitise their debt by converting it into asset-backed securities.

These bonds are then transferred to the government as collateral. The company must pay off the tax debt and accumulated funds in regular instalments, and if it falls behind the government can sell the bonds.

A government order earlier this year allows companies to restructure tax debts either by issuing the bonds or by issuing new equity comprising a controlling stake, to be held as collateral by the state.
Khodorkovsky said total debts of Rosprom-YUKOS's subsidiaries, including Yuganskneftegaz, and counting all fines on debt, came to 12 trillion roubles.
YUKOS president Sergei Muravlenko said a formal decision on issuing bonds on Yuganskneftegaz's debt had already been made and that the process was already underway.
"We will gradually apply the same decisions to other subsidiaries, the first of which will be Samaraneftegaz," Muravlenko said.
Khodorkovsky said a government commission was currently discussing the Yuganskneftegaz bond issue and would set the volume and maturity of the bonds.
